channel.description: Latest articles from UK Defence Journal (ukdefencejournal.org.uk)

item.title: Army reserve in major explosion response drill near Glasgow
item.description: Personnel from 144 (Parachute) Medical Squadron, an Army Reserve unit that forms part of 16 Medical Regiment, have taken part in a large-scale emergency response exercise near Glasgow. The post Army reserve in major explosion response drill near Glasgow first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: NATO military staff chief visits alliance sites in Italy
item.description: Lieutenant General Remigijus Baltrėnas, Director General of the International Military Staff, has completed a two-day visit to several NATO structures in Italy, including facilities in Naples and Rome. The post NATO military staff chief visits alliance sites in Italy first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Delta Force won’t invade Greenland; but Wall Street might
item.description: Claims that the United States could seek to seize Greenland misunderstand both geography and strategy, with Washington far more likely to deepen influence through investment and cooperation as Arctic routes and critical minerals grow in importance, argues former MP and defence commentator James Gray. The post Delta Force won’t invade Greenland; but Wall Street might first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Sweeney warns vessel delays risk shipyard job losses
item.description: "The Scottish Government have failed to purchase a new vessel with a Scottish shipyard in over a decade," warned Paul Sweeney MSP. The post Sweeney warns vessel delays risk shipyard job losses first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK Defence Journal reporting on Iran bots raised in inquiry
item.description: A House of Commons committee heard evidence that bot activity linked to Iran appeared to drop sharply during internet shutdowns inside the country, with UK Defence Journal reporting referenced in the discussion. The post UK Defence Journal reporting on Iran bots raised in inquiry first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Why the Proteus autonomous helicopter matters
item.description: The first flight of the Royal Navy's Proteus autonomous helicopter is a visible milestone, but the aircraft's importance lies less in the airframe and more in the operational pressure that led to its development. The post Why the Proteus autonomous helicopter matters first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: QinetiQ secures huge Typhoon support contract extension
item.description: The agreement will see QinetiQ deliver ongoing mission-critical engineering support intended to sustain Typhoon capability and pilot safety. The post QinetiQ secures huge Typhoon support contract extension first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK draws red line on Greenland sovereignty
item.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer has warned that the use of trade tariffs against allied nations is "completely wrong", after US President Donald Trump said he would impose sweeping import taxes on countries opposing his proposal for the United States to acquire Greenland. The post UK draws red line on Greenland sovereignty first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Avenger jet drone conducts simulated intercept
item.description: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems has completed another autonomous flight demonstration using its MQ-20 Avenger jet, including a simulated aerial intercept against a live, piloted aircraft, according to the company. The post Avenger jet drone conducts simulated intercept first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: US warship fires weapons during South China Sea patrol
item.description: A U.S. Navy destroyer has carried out live-fire training while operating in the South China Sea as part of routine deployment activity with a carrier strike group, according to the service. The post US warship fires weapons during South China Sea patrol first appeared on UK Defence Journal.
